question_bank.stem: Montezuma's Revenge is hard for a randomly initialized RL agent because useful reward depends on what kind of behavior?

options.text: A long sequence of prior-informed actions before reward appears
A single immediate reward visible from the first state
A complete table of legal moves supplied by the game
A continuous steering angle predicted at every frame

question_bank.rationale: The instructor points to actions like using a rope and ladder, which humans recognize but a random agent is unlikely to discover early.

distractor_rationales.B: The example is difficult because the reward is delayed, not immediate.
distractor_rationales.C: The game does not provide a solved move table to the agent.
distractor_rationales.D: Continuous steering is used to motivate PPO, not Montezuma's sparse reward.

frame_evidence.description: Slide compares Atari games and shows Montezuma's Revenge as a sparse-reward task requiring human-like priors.

question_bank.stem: PPO is introduced as more suitable than a one-output-per-action DQN when the action space has what property?

options.text: Continuous controls such as steering angles

question_bank.rationale: The lecture contrasts DQN's discrete action outputs with continuous actions like turning a wheel, for which PPO is preferred.

distractor_rationales.A: Two discrete actions are compatible with simple DQN outputs.
distractor_rationales.B: Sparse terminal reward is a challenge but not the continuous-action reason for PPO here.
distractor_rationales.D: Full observability is not what makes PPO preferable in this example.

source_ref.evidence_span: If you actually have a game that has continuous action,

frame_evidence.description: Advanced topics slide lists PPO/TRPO and contrasts policy methods with value-based Q-learning.

question_bank.stem: Compared with Q-learning, PPO is introduced as a method that does not primarily learn what object before choosing an action?

options.text: A scalar reward head for human preference
A value table used with an argmax policy
A cropped stack of Breakout screen frames
A replay memory of consecutive experiences

question_bank.rationale: The lecture contrasts PPO/TRPO with value-based Q-learning, where Q-values are learned and a policy is defined by argmax over those values.

distractor_rationales.A: A scalar reward head belongs to RLHF reward modeling, not PPO's contrast with Q-learning.
distractor_rationales.C: Breakout frame stacks are DQN input preprocessing, not the value-based object being contrasted.
distractor_rationales.D: Replay memory stabilizes DQN training but is not the Q-value object used for argmax.

source_ref.evidence_span: it is not a value-based algorithm.
